newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 30.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* SBC Communications Inc Chairman Edward Whitacre called off merger talks with AT&T by, appropriately enough, placing a call to his counterpart at the telecommunications giant.
* Hostile takeover bids may have gained legitimacy, but they are becoming even harder to win, an analysis has found.
* Gross Domestic Product rose at an annual rate of 5.9 percent in the first quarter.
* Corporate profits are expected to increase by high single digits to low double digits in the second quarter.
* J.P. Morgan is in talks to acquire 45 percent of American Century, a mutual fund company, for $900 million, sources said.
* Raytheon appears likely to secure approval from the U.S. Justice Department for its $3 billion buyout of Texas Instruments defense business, if it sells or licenses key chip-making technology.
* Julian Robertson is considering selling a stake in Tiger Management that would value Tiger at more than $6 billion.
* PacifiCare Health Systems Inc warned that its second-quarter earnings would be less than half of what most analysts were forecasting.
* Texaco Inc's former treasurer was indicted on charges he planned to destroy documents related to a race-discrimination lawsuit against the company.
* The Federal Communications Commission is expected to issue a license for the Ellipso global-satellite telephone system proposed by closely held Mobile Communications.
* NationsBank Corp is expected to announce a deal to acquire Montomery Securities Inc for about $1.2 billion in cash and stock.
* PepsiCo plans to scrap its agreement to distribute Ocean Spray drinks next year, perhaps portending a move to develop its own line of juices.
* Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc plans to increase its stake in Grupo Modelo SA de CV, acquiring an addition 13.25 percent direct and indirect interest in the Mexican brewer.
* Royal Bank of Canada has agreed to acquire London Insurance Group for $1.74 billion.
* Northeast Utilities failed to receive authority from Connecticut regulators to increase electricity rates to help cover losses from its idled Millstone nuclear power plants.

* Heard on the Street: Microsoft, as it invests in a myriad of interactive and high-tech television businesses in an effort to diversify and prepare for the future, might learn a few lessons from IBM, itself a wealthy giant of the 1980s.
* Credit Markets: Bond-market participants are split on whether bonds can extend their recent rally even as nearly no one expects the Federal Reserve to move to increase rates.
